---
title: "Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM)"
subtitle: "A cited reconstruction from bibliographic evidence and later accounts"
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Scope of this chapter
This page reconstructs what public sources now support about the Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM). It uses one inspected late-1990s bibliography for the 1990 manual, later organizational and training accounts for the project name, and an inspected 1994 Van der Klift publication that is **not** an ECPM manual. It does **not** treat ECPM as a proven formal predecessor of CSIL. The 1990 manual itself has not been read. A distinct 1994 ECPM training manual remains an open identity question.
:::

## How this chapter uses evidence

Statements below are labelled as one of:

- **Documented (bibliographic)** — a cited finding aid attests title, creators, date, or physical description; this archive has not seen the work itself
- **Documented (inspected later source)** — taken from a later page or deck that was read
- **Attributed recollection** — a later named account; this archive is not independently asserting it
- **Interpretation** — inferred from those sources, and said to be so
- **Open question** — not settled by inspected evidence

Contemporaneous or bibliographic evidence is preferred when later accounts differ. Later IFRC and Gauthier wording is not treated as a 1990s ministry instrument.

## What ECPM can be documented as

The strongest independently verifiable public description is bibliographic, not a recovered manual.

The [Roeher Institute / Brian Salisbury annotated bibliography](../sources/1990s-roeher-if-bibliography.qmd) (inspected PDF of a late-1990s finding aid) lists:

> BC Rehab & Greater Vancouver Home Support Society  
> “Enhanced Consumer Participation Model: Skill Development Manual for Consumers of Home Support Services”, BC Rehab & Greater Vancouver Home Support Society, 1990  
> A training manual that includes 5 modules intended to empower consumers to act as effective employers (52 pages plus appendices)

**Documented (bibliographic):** a 1990 skill-development manual existed under the ECPM name; it was issued by BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society; it had five modules and was described as training consumers to act as employers.

**What that citation does not show.** The bibliography does not name personal authors, a place of publication, an ISBN, a revision history, or a relationship to CSIL. This archive has not inspected the manual and must not paraphrase unretrieved module contents.

Later sources use “ECPM” as a **named project**, not only as a manual title:

- [IFRC “Our Team”](../sources/ifrc-our-team.qmd) (inspected later organizational page) calls ECPM “the individual funding project” that preceded CSIL.
- [Gauthier 2014](../sources/2014-gauthier-sci-csil-presentation.qmd) (inspected later training deck) lists “ECPM Enhanced Consumer Participation Model” under “Pre CSIL?” with “The Agency” and “People paid themselves.”

Those are **attributed later reconstructions**. They support treating ECPM as a name later writers attach to a pre-CSIL individualized-funding arrangement. They do not supply a contemporaneous program regulation, contract, or ministry instrument.

Current [Vancouver Coastal Health CSIL service pages](../sources/vch-csil-service-page.qmd) do **not** use the ECPM name. Institutional survival of the acronym at VCH is not documented.

## Organizations and people supported by evidence

| Person or body | What inspected evidence supports | What it does not support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BC Rehab / BC Rehabilitation Society | Corporate author of the 1990 manual in Roeher | Personal editors; legal continuity into later health authorities |
| Greater Vancouver Home Support Society | Co-author of the 1990 manual in Roeher | A recovered GVHSS file; later VCH succession as an ECPM office |
| [Joseph Theriault](../people/joseph-theriault.qmd) | IFRC later wording: worked with Paul Gauthier and others on the individual-funding project “then known as” ECPM | Any name on the unread 1990 title page; a contemporaneous job title |
| [Paul Gauthier](../people/paul-gauthier.qmd) | Later IFRC/Gauthier materials place him in a pre-CSIL / CSIL founding story that *names* ECPM | A contemporaneous ECPM appointment; authorship of the 1990 manual |
| [Emma Van der Klift](../people/emma-van-der-klift.qmd) | Author, with Norman Kunc, of a **different** 1994 chapter ([*Hell-Bent on Helping*](../sources/1994-van-der-klift-hell-bent.qmd)) | Authorship of a 1994 ECPM training manual; any inspected ECPM credit |
| Vancouver Health Department | Named only in the commissioning issue / research brief as a possible 1994-manual affiliate | Any inspected 1990s document using that affiliation for ECPM |

: Documented and excluded ECPM roles, from inspected sources only

No inspected source names a design committee or proves that any of these people sat on a later CSIL design group **because of** ECPM. Design-group membership is not inferred here.

Search-engine restatements of the Roeher entry are **not** counted as independent confirmation. Experiment 001 treated this item as bibliographically attested and unread.

## The unresolved 1994-manual question

A possible 1994 ECPM training revision appears in the commissioning issue and later research brief. It is **not** listed in the inspected Roeher bibliography. No public full text, catalogue holding, or second independent citation was recovered.

[Van der Klift and Kunc, “Hell-Bent on Helping” (1994)](../sources/1994-van-der-klift-hell-bent.qmd) is a published chapter on help and inclusive education. The inspected Broadreach republication does **not** name ECPM, CSIL, BC Rehab, Greater Vancouver Home Support Society, or Vancouver Health Department. It is a **near-miss**: a real 1994 Van der Klift publication from the same year as the hypothesized manual, not bibliographic evidence that she wrote or revised an ECPM text.

**Archive status (Experiment 001 conclusion, used here as research input):** **INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE** to decide whether the reported 1994 item is a distinct work, a revision of the 1990 manual, a conflicting citation of the same 1990 work, or a confusion with *Hell-Bent on Helping*.

This is not yet a contradiction between two inspected bibliographic records. It is one inspected 1990 citation versus later uncited project notes.

## Relationship to later CSIL

| Claim | Status | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Later IFRC wording treats ECPM as the individual-funding project that preceded CSIL | Attributed recollection | [IFRC Our Team](../sources/ifrc-our-team.qmd) |
| Later Gauthier slides list ECPM as a “Pre CSIL?” step | Attributed recollection | [Gauthier 2014](../sources/2014-gauthier-sci-csil-presentation.qmd) |
| Creekview became ECPM, or ECPM became CSIL, by a formal instrument | Open question | No inspected 1990s instrument says so. The [Creekview chapter](creekview.qmd) does not establish that link. |
| Current VCH pages continue the ECPM name | Not supported | [VCH CSIL page](../sources/vch-csil-service-page.qmd) |

: What later sources say about ECPM and CSIL — not a proven succession

**Interpretation, and no further:** ECPM is a named 1990 training/manual project (bibliographically) and a named pre-CSIL individualized-funding idea in later participant/organizational accounts. Those two uses may describe the same effort, related efforts, or a later label applied to earlier work. This archive does **not** convert that overlap into a proven formal succession.

[*Keys on Freedom*](../sources/wanted-keys-on-freedom.qmd) remains unconfirmed (title/author/year still commissioning-issue only). Roeher does not list it. No relationship to the 1990 ECPM manual is established.

## Unresolved questions

1. Full text, title-page authors, place, ISBN, and module titles of the 1990 manual.
2. Whether a 1994 ECPM training manual exists as a distinct document.
3. Whether Van der Klift, Theriault, Gauthier, GVHSS staff, or Vancouver Health Department appear on any ECPM title page.
4. What contemporaneous program, contract, or agency arrangement “ECPM” named besides the manual.
5. Whether *Keys on Freedom* is related, identical in purpose, or unrelated.
6. Whether any 1990s Ministry of Health file uses the ECPM name in connection with CSIL design.

Recovery of the manuals belongs with [Issue #5](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/csil-history/issues/5) and [Issue #6](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/csil-history/issues/6). Leads are listed on the [wanted ECPM manuals record](../sources/wanted-ecpm-manuals.qmd).
